steps.intent: Our primary objectives are to secure a one-year renewal of MINURSO's mandate while decisively locking in Morocco's Autonomy Proposal as the primary and most realistic basis for a political settlement, alongside advancing transition planning for the mission's eventual drawdown. The main points of friction during negotiations will be Russia's expected objections to elevating the Moroccan autonomy framework over the traditional referendum option, potential language disputes regarding Algeria's direct inclusion as a party, and pushback against initiating MINURSO transition planning before a final political settlement is formally signed.

messages.Bahrain: The Kingdom of Bahrain commends the United States for preparing a robust, realistic, and forward-looking draft resolution that accurately reflects the growing international momentum behind the Moroccan Autonomy Initiative. Bahrain reaffirms its steadfast and unequivocal support for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Kingdom of Morocco over the Moroccan Sahara, viewing the Moroccan proposal as the sole serious and credible basis to achieve a definitive political solution. We fully support the draft text as presented and stand ready to vote in favor of its adoption.
messages.China: China has consistently supported the mandate renewal of MINURSO, which plays an indispensable role in maintaining stability on the ground and creating conditions for a political settlement. However, the Council's resolutions must maintain neutrality and balance, reflecting the legitimate concerns and proposals of all parties rather than prejudging the outcome of negotiations or the exercise of self-determination. We urge the penholder to conduct thorough and transparent consultations to forge the broadest possible consensus among Council members.
messages.Colombia: Colombia reaffirms its steadfast commitment to international law and the fundamental, inalienable right of the people of Western Sahara to self-determination. Council resolutions must maintain a balanced approach and not prejudge the outcome of political negotiations by presenting autonomy under Moroccan sovereignty as the sole permissible endpoint. Furthermore, MINURSO's peacekeeping presence remains indispensable for regional stability and monitoring the ceasefire, and premature moves toward mission drawdown or transition risk undermining the political process.
messages.Democratic Republic of the Congo: The Democratic Republic of the Congo fully supports the draft resolution submitted by the United States and welcomes the one-year extension of MINURSO's mandate. We reaffirm our firm backing for Morocco's Autonomy Proposal as the only credible, realistic, and pragmatic basis for achieving a definitive and mutually acceptable political solution. We commend the penholder for reflecting the growing international momentum toward this outcome and stand ready to vote in favor of the text as drafted.
messages.Denmark: Denmark strongly supports the extension of MINURSO's mandate and the mediation efforts led by Personal Envoy Staffan de Mistura, viewing Morocco's autonomy proposal as a serious and credible basis for negotiations. However, it is essential that the resolution upholds the principle of self-determination and does not prejudge the outcome of talks or formally prejudge sovereignty before an agreement is reached between the parties. Furthermore, given ongoing tensions on the ground, MINURSO remains indispensable for monitoring and regional stability; language pointing toward premature transition planning should be avoided.
messages.France: France warmly welcomes the draft resolution circulated by the United States, which appropriately reflects the growing international momentum behind Morocco's 2007 Autonomy Plan. For France, the present and future of Western Sahara lie within the framework of Moroccan sovereignty, and genuine autonomy under Moroccan sovereignty is the only viable, credible, and realistic basis for a just and lasting political settlement. We fully support the renewal of MINURSO's mandate and stand ready to vote in favour of the text as drafted.
messages.Greece: Greece commends the United States for its leadership as penholder and fully supports the extension of MINURSO's mandate as an indispensable pillar of regional stability. We view Morocco's Autonomy Proposal as a serious and credible basis for advancing the political process, while emphasizing that an enduring, viable solution must be anchored in genuine negotiations, the UN Charter, and international law. Our suggested adjustments seek to maintain continuity with Council precedent and facilitate broader consensus among members.
messages.Latvia: Latvia welcomes the draft resolution circulated by the United States extending MINURSO's mandate for an additional year and reaffirms its full support for Personal Envoy Staffan de Mistura's efforts to facilitate substantive negotiations. We view Morocco's Autonomy Proposal as a serious, realistic, and credible basis to advance the political process toward a just, lasting, and mutually acceptable solution in line with the principles of the UN Charter. We appreciate the penholder's leadership in preserving the momentum of the political track while ensuring the continued operational effectiveness of MINURSO.
messages.Liberia: Liberia expresses its full support for the draft resolution submitted by the United States. We welcome the clear reaffirmation of Morocco’s Autonomy Proposal as the only credible, realistic, and viable framework to achieve a definitive and mutually acceptable political solution. Liberia also endorses the extension of MINURSO's mandate and supports aligning the mission's operational posture with the positive momentum in the political process.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan attaches high importance to resolving the question of Western Sahara peacefully, in accordance with UN principles and the fraternal ties we share with the parties involved. However, the cardinal principle of self-determination is sacrosanct under the UN Charter and international law, and Council resolutions must not prejudge or constrain the outcome of negotiations to an autonomy framework. We urge the penholder to restore balance by preserving genuine self-determination and accommodating the positions of all parties so as to foster consensus.
messages.Panama: Panama appreciates the United States' leadership as penholder and fully supports the renewal of MINURSO's mandate to bolster the political process led by Personal Envoy Staffan de Mistura. We continue to regard Morocco’s 2007 Autonomy Proposal as a serious and suitable basis for advancing towards a just, lasting, and mutually acceptable solution. To preserve Council cohesion and honor the fundamental principle of self-determination under the UN Charter—a principle of profound historical significance to Panama—we suggest minor adjustments to OP3 to retain balanced language from previous resolutions.
messages.Russian Federation: The draft resolution once again reflects an unbalanced approach that seeks to predetermine the outcome of negotiations by imposing a single option and redefining the principle of self-determination. Furthermore, attempting to initiate transition planning to phase out MINURSO in the absence of a viable political settlement undermines regional stability and the Mission's core mandate. The Russian Federation urges the penholder to abandon unilateral national agendas, respect the agreed international legal framework, and return to balanced language that accommodates the views of all parties.
messages.Somalia: Somalia fully supports the draft resolution presented by the United States to extend MINURSO's mandate for another year. We welcome the emphasis on Morocco's Autonomy Proposal as a serious, credible, and realistic basis to achieve a just, lasting, and mutually acceptable political solution under UN auspices. We commend the penholder for maintaining diplomatic momentum and urge all invited parties to engage constructively and in good faith with the Personal Envoy.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom strongly supports the US penholder's leadership and the momentum reflected in this text, which appropriately recognizes Morocco's autonomy proposal as a credible and pragmatic basis for resolving this protracted dispute. We welcome the forward-looking focus on MINURSO's transition following the strategic review. To ensure broad Council support and maintain consistency with established Charter principles, we propose maintaining our standard reference to the self-determination of the people of Western Sahara in OP3 alongside autonomy, and retaining the Council's customary call for cooperation with OHCHR.

messages.Bahrain: The Kingdom of Bahrain expresses its full support for the draft resolution circulated by the United States. We particularly welcome the reaffirmed recognition of Morocco's serious and credible Autonomy Proposal under Moroccan sovereignty as the most feasible and realistic basis for a lasting political settlement, alongside the emphasis on refugee registration in the Tindouf camps. Bahrain stands ready to vote in favour of the text without further modification.
messages.China: China appreciates the penholder's revisions to address concerns regarding the language on self-determination in OP3. However, the draft text remains unbalanced by exclusively foregrounding one party's proposal in PP5 and OP2 while omitting the proposals of the other party. To facilitate broad Council consensus and support an impartial political process, the resolution must remain balanced and reflect the legitimate concerns of all relevant parties; otherwise, China will not be in a position to support it.
messages.Colombia: Colombia thanks the penholder for addressing our core concern in OP3 regarding the self-determination of the people of Western Sahara, as well as the adjustments made to OP4. To ensure a truly balanced text that does not prejudge the outcome of negotiations or undermine the principle of self-determination, we urge the penholder to adopt more neutral formulations in PP5 and OP2 regarding the basis and potential outcomes of the political process.
messages.Democratic Republic of the Congo: The Democratic Republic of the Congo fully supports the draft resolution as presented by the penholder. We commend the balanced text, which appropriately extends MINURSO's mandate while reaffirming Morocco's Autonomy Initiative as a serious, credible, and realistic framework for achieving a definitive political solution. We stand ready to vote in favor of this draft.
messages.Denmark: Denmark expresses its sincere appreciation to the penholder for incorporating our proposed adjustments into Revision 1. The draft strikes an appropriate balance by ensuring MINURSO's continued operational role, supporting the efforts of Personal Envoy Staffan de Mistura, and preserving the principle of self-determination in accordance with the Charter of the United Nations. Denmark fully supports the text as currently drafted and is ready to vote in favor.
messages.France: France fully supports the draft resolution as prepared by the United States. The text accurately reflects the political momentum, properly highlights Morocco's Autonomy Proposal as the credible framework under Moroccan sovereignty to achieve a just and lasting solution, and ensures MINURSO's continued essential role on the ground. We stand ready to vote in favour of the text without further amendment.
messages.Greece: Greece thanks the United States for incorporating our proposals into revision 1, notably the reference to international law and balanced language regarding self-determination. The current text strikes a sound balance in advancing the political process under the Personal Envoy while ensuring MINURSO's continued operational role. Greece fully supports the draft resolution as presented and looks forward to voting in favor.
messages.Latvia: Latvia welcomes revision 1 and thanks the United States for maintaining a standard 12-month extension for MINURSO and preserving full support for Personal Envoy Staffan de Mistura. We appreciate the draft's balanced emphasis on a realistic, compromise-based political solution consistent with the UN Charter, as well as the important language regarding MINURSO's freedom of movement, ceasefire adherence, and humanitarian needs. Latvia is prepared to vote in favor of this draft resolution as presented.
messages.Liberia: Liberia fully supports the draft resolution as presented by the United States. The text provides a balanced and realistic framework that rightly recognizes Morocco's Autonomy Proposal as the credible basis for achieving a definitive, lasting political solution, while renewing MINURSO's critical mandate. We encourage all Council members to support this text without further amendments.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan appreciates the penholder's efforts and the adjustments made to OP3; however, the current draft continues to tilt negotiations by prejudging their outcome. For Pakistan, the cardinal principle of self-determination enshrined in the UN Charter is sacrosanct and must not be circumscribed or predetermined. Unless the text is balanced to reflect the positions of all parties without prescribing autonomy as the sole feasible end state, Pakistan will not be able to vote in favour of the resolution.
messages.Panama: Panama thanks the United States for incorporating our suggested language in operative paragraph 3, which appropriately reflects both the right to self-determination and the realistic prospects offered by genuine autonomy. The revised draft strikes a constructive and balanced approach in support of Personal Envoy de Mistura's efforts to reach a just, lasting, and mutually acceptable political solution. Panama is pleased with the text as presented and stands ready to vote in favour.
messages.Russian Federation: While we note the adjustments made in revision 1, the draft remains fundamentally unbalanced by attempting to predetermine the outcome of negotiations and elevate one party's proposal over agreed United Nations parameters. Furthermore, introducing language aimed at reviewing MINURSO's future footprint risks prematurely undermining the Mission's stabilizing presence before a mutually acceptable settlement is reached. Unless the text is returned to balanced, neutral language reflecting all parties' proposals and the established framework for self-determination, the Russian Federation will be obliged to abstain.
messages.Somalia: Somalia fully supports the draft resolution as presented by the United States and appreciates the penholder's balanced and constructive leadership. The text appropriately reinforces the momentum behind a realistic, pragmatic, and lasting political solution, emphasizing Morocco's Autonomy Proposal as a credible framework under UN auspices. We support the one-year extension of MINURSO's mandate and stand ready to vote in favor of the resolution.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom thanks the United States for incorporating our suggested language on self-determination in operative paragraph 3 and on cooperation with OHCHR in preambular paragraph 7. The revised draft strikes an appropriate and constructive balance, reflecting the momentum behind Morocco's autonomy proposal as a credible and viable basis for progress while preserving the core principles of the political process and MINURSO's vital role. We fully support this text and look forward to voting in favour of its adoption.

steps.summary: As penholder, the United States has put forward Revision 1 in blue without further changes, consolidating the broad support of eleven Council members behind a standard 12-month renewal of MINURSO. The draft firmly anchors negotiations in Morocco's Autonomy Proposal as the only credible, realistic framework for peace while respecting the UN Charter and the principle of self-determination. The Council will comfortably adopt the resolution with 11 affirmative votes, with China, Colombia, Pakistan, and Russia expected to abstain.

reasons.Bahrain: Bahrain steadfastly supports the territorial integrity and sovereignty of the Kingdom of Morocco over Western Sahara and regards the Moroccan Autonomy Initiative as the only serious, realistic, and credible basis for resolving this dispute, fully justifying a vote in favour of the draft resolution.
reasons.China: Consistent with our position on Resolution 2797 (2025), China abstains because the draft resolution continues to lack balance, elevating one party's proposal while disregarding the legitimate concerns and proposals of other parties despite our constructive amendment requests during consultations.
reasons.Colombia: Colombia abstained because the draft resolution unequivocally prioritizes Morocco's Autonomy Proposal and predetermines the outcome of the political process, running counter to the fundamental right of the Sahrawi people to self-determination and the principle of neutrality enshrined in the Charter of the United Nations. Having had its constructive amendments rejected, Colombia cannot endorse an unbalanced political framework while still recognizing the operational value of MINURSO.
reasons.Democratic Republic of the Congo: The Democratic Republic of the Congo firmly supports Morocco's sovereignty and territorial integrity, recognizes the Moroccan Autonomy Proposal as the only credible and realistic framework for resolving the dispute, and supports the renewal of MINURSO's mandate to maintain regional stability.
reasons.Denmark: Denmark supports the 12-month renewal of MINURSO's mandate to maintain stability on the ground and fully backs the UN-led political process guided by Personal Envoy Staffan de Mistura. Consistent with its vote on resolution 2797 (2025) and established Council practice, Denmark votes in favour and reserves any explanation of vote for after the adoption.
reasons.France: France fully supports the draft resolution renewing MINURSO's mandate, which aligns directly with France's policy recognizing Moroccan sovereignty and the 2007 Autonomy Plan as the only credible basis for a lasting settlement. As is standard practice, France will vote in favour and deliver any remarks after the vote.
reasons.Greece: Greece consistently supports the renewal of MINURSO's mandate and the UN-led political process under the auspices of the Secretary-General and his Personal Envoy. The draft resolution appropriately reflects international law, the UN Charter, and the need for a realistic, mutually acceptable political solution based on compromise.
reasons.Latvia: Latvia supports the 12-month renewal of MINURSO's mandate and the UN-led political process under Personal Envoy Staffan de Mistura, aligning closely with EU and transatlantic partners. Having supported the draft text in negotiations, Latvia votes in favour and reserves any remarks for after the vote.
reasons.Liberia: Liberia strongly supports Morocco's sovereignty and territorial integrity, views the Moroccan Autonomy Initiative as the only serious and credible basis for a lasting resolution, and fully supports extending MINURSO's mandate.
reasons.Pakistan: The draft resolution maintains the unbalanced language prioritizing Morocco's Autonomy Proposal over a genuine, unconstrained exercise of the right to self-determination, directly infringing upon Pakistan's red lines and principled stance, consistent with our abstention on Resolution 2797 in 2025.
reasons.Panama: Panama supports the renewal of MINURSO's mandate and the balanced text put forward by the penholder, which reflects Morocco's autonomy proposal as a viable basis while upholding the principle of self-determination in accordance with the UN Charter.
reasons.Russian Federation: In line with our established voting record on MINURSO mandate renewals, Russia abstains due to the unbalanced nature of the text, which prejudges the outcome of negotiations by prioritizing Morocco's autonomy plan over a mutually acceptable solution that guarantees the self-determination of the people of Western Sahara. The penholder once again disregarded our constructive proposals, but Russia chooses to abstain rather than veto to preserve MINURSO's operational presence on the ground.
reasons.Somalia: Somalia strongly supports the extension of MINURSO's mandate and the US-drafted text affirming Morocco's Autonomy Proposal as a credible and realistic basis for a lasting solution, consistent with our vote on resolution 2797 and our established bilateral and regional policy. In accordance with Council practice, we will deliver any national remarks after the adoption rather than before the vote.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports the renewal of MINURSO's mandate and the US-drafted resolution, which aligns with our position viewing Morocco's autonomy proposal as a credible and pragmatic basis for a solution while upholding the principle of self-determination, and we will deliver our statement after the vote.
reasons.United States of America: As the penholder and author of the draft resolution, the United States strongly supports the text, which reflects US policy recognizing Morocco's autonomy proposal as the most viable path toward resolving the dispute and extends MINURSO's mandate.

before.United States of America:
Thank you, Mr. President. 

The United States is proud to put forward this draft resolution to extend the mandate of MINURSO for another year. For decades, the dispute over Western Sahara has remained unresolved, impacting regional stability and human lives. Today, we have a real opportunity to sustain the diplomatic momentum generated over the past year and move decisively toward a durable political solution.

This resolution reaffirms the Security Council's steadfast support for the Personal Envoy of the Secretary-General, Staffan de Mistura, as he works to bring the parties together for substantive negotiations. It recognizes Morocco’s serious, credible, and realistic Autonomy Proposal as the most feasible framework to achieve a just, lasting, and mutually acceptable solution that satisfies the aspirations of the people of Western Sahara. 

At the same time, this draft underlines our continued commitment to MINURSO’s essential role in preserving stability on the ground, ensuring the safety of UN personnel, and enabling the political track to succeed. We have consulted extensively with all members of this Council to produce a text that is balanced, forward-looking, and focused on tangible progress.

We urge all members of the Council to vote in favor of this draft resolution and demonstrate our collective resolve to achieve lasting peace in the region. Thank you.

after.Bahrain:
Mr. President,

The delegation of the Kingdom of Bahrain welcomed the adoption of the resolution extending the mandate of the United Nations Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara (MINURSO) until 31 October 2027, and we thank the United States, as penholder, for its efforts in facilitating this text.

Bahrain’s vote in favour reflects our firm and principled position, under the leadership of His Majesty King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa, in steadfast support of the territorial integrity and national sovereignty of the brotherly Kingdom of Morocco over the entirety of its territory, including the Moroccan Sahara. This commitment was tangibly demonstrated by the opening of the Consulate General of the Kingdom of Bahrain in the city of Laayoune.

My delegation reaffirms its full support for the Moroccan Autonomy Initiative presented in 2007, which has garnered extensive and growing international support as a serious, realistic, and credible basis for achieving a definitive, just, and lasting political solution to this regional dispute, in full respect of Morocco’s sovereignty and territorial integrity.

We reiterate our support for the efforts of the Secretary-General and his Personal Envoy, Mr. Staffan de Mistura, to advance the political process in accordance with the relevant Security Council resolutions. We call on all parties to engage constructively and in good faith, without preconditions, taking the Moroccan Autonomy Initiative as the framework for negotiations, with a view to reaching a pragmatic and mutually acceptable solution that fosters security, stability, and integration across the Maghreb and the wider region.

Finally, we underline the imperative of addressing the humanitarian situation in the Tindouf camps, reiterating the call for the formal registration and census of the population residing there, in accordance with international humanitarian law and relevant United Nations resolutions.

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.China:
Mr. President,

China has always supported the work of the United Nations Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara (MINURSO). Over the years, MINURSO has diligently fulfilled its mandate as authorized by the Security Council, playing an important role in monitoring the ceasefire, conducting mine clearance, and maintaining regional peace and stability, thereby creating necessary conditions for advancing the political process. China supports the extension of MINURSO’s mandate.

China’s position on the question of Western Sahara is consistent and clear. We have always maintained that a political solution is the only viable path. We support a just, lasting, and mutually acceptable solution reached through equal-footed dialogue and consultations between the parties on the basis of the relevant Security Council resolutions, consistent with the purposes and principles of the Charter of the United Nations. China also supports the Secretary-General and his Personal Envoy, Mr. Staffan de Mistura, in continuing their mediation efforts to revitalize the political process.

During the consultations on the draft resolution, China, along with other Council members, put forward constructive suggestions with a view to improving the text, making it more balanced and objective, and accommodating the legitimate concerns of all parties. Regrettably, the resolution just adopted failed to fully reflect the legitimate concerns of all parties involved and did not adequately incorporate the views of Council members. The text remains unbalanced. Consequently, China had to abstain in the voting.

China hopes that going forward, the penholder will adopt an open, transparent, and constructive attitude, engage in thorough and meaningful consultations with all Council members, and accommodate the concerns of all sides so as to build broader consensus. China stands ready to continue to play a constructive role in facilitating an early, comprehensive, and just settlement of the question of Western Sahara.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.Colombia:
Mr. President,

Colombia abstained on the resolution just adopted, and I wish to briefly explain the reasons for our vote.

Colombia reaffirms its steadfast commitment to the principles and purposes of the Charter of the United Nations, international law, and the fundamental right of peoples to self-determination, as enshrined in General Assembly resolution 1514 (XV). In this spirit, we have consistently supported the efforts of the Secretary-General and his Personal Envoy, Mr. Staffan de Mistura, to achieve a just, lasting, and mutually acceptable political solution to the question of Western Sahara.

We also recognize the indispensable role played by the United Nations Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara (MINURSO) as an instrument of peace, ceasefire monitoring, and regional stability. It is for this reason that Colombia did not oppose the extension of the Mission’s mandate.

However, Colombia could not support the resolution as drafted. The text presented before us departs from the necessary balance and neutrality that must guide this Council's action. By preconditioning negotiations and privileging one single proposal over others, the resolution risks predetermining the outcome of a process that belongs first and foremost to the Sahrawi people. A genuine and lasting peace cannot be built by constraining the democratic choice of the population concerned; self-determination cannot be substituted or predefined without their free and authentic will.

Furthermore, we regret that the resolution misses an important opportunity to strengthen the Mission's mandate regarding the independent monitoring and protection of human rights in the territory, as well as addressing the urgent humanitarian situation of the Sahrawi refugees.

Colombia reiterates its call on the parties—the Kingdom of Morocco and the Frente POLISARIO—to resume substantive, direct, and unconditional negotiations in good faith. Our vote today is a vote in defense of international law, the historical mandate of the United Nations, and the inalienable right of the Sahrawi people to freely decide their own destiny.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.Democratic Republic of the Congo:
Monsieur le Président,

La République démocratique du Congo salue l'adoption de la résolution qui vient de renouveler pour un an le mandat de la Mission des Nations Unies pour l'organisation d'un référendum au Sahara occidental (MINURSO). Notre vote favorable témoigne de notre attachement constant à la paix, à la stabilité régionale et au règlement pacifique des différends par la voie du dialogue et de la négociation.

Ma délégation réitère son plein soutien aux efforts déployés par le Secrétaire général et son Envoyé personnel, M. Staffan de Mistura, visant à relancer et faire progresser le processus politique sous l'égide exclusive des Nations Unies, afin de parvenir à une solution politique juste, durable et mutuellement acceptable à ce différend régional qui n'a que trop duré.

À cet égard, la République démocratique du Congo réaffirme son appui indéfectible à l'Initiative marocaine d'autonomie présentée en 2007. Cette initiative constitue une base sérieuse, crédible et pragmatique, pleinement conforme à la légalité internationale et aux résolutions pertinentes du Conseil de sécurité, susceptible d'offrir une perspective réaliste et viable pour le règlement définitif de cette question, dans le respect de la souveraineté et de l'intégrité territoriale du Royaume du Maroc.

Nous appelons l'ensemble des parties concernées — le Maroc, le Front POLISARIO, l'Algérie et la Mauritanie — à faire preuve de volonté politique, à dépasser les postures de blocage et à s'engager de bonne foi, dans un esprit de compromis et sans conditions préalables, dans les pourparlers menés par l'Envoyé personnel, en tirant parti de la dynamique positive actuelle.

Enfin, la République démocratique du Congo tient à rendre hommage au personnel civil et militaire de la MINURSO pour son travail remarquable sur le terrain dans des conditions exigeantes, et appelle à garantir à la Mission la liberté de mouvement et les moyens logistiques nécessaires à la bonne exécution de son mandat, qui demeure essentiel pour le maintien du cessez-le-feu et de la stabilité dans toute la région.

Je vous remercie, Monsieur le Président.
after.Denmark:
Thank you, Mr. President.

Denmark voted in favour of the resolution just adopted, extending the mandate of MINURSO for a further 12 months. 

We did so first and foremost in recognition of MINURSO’s indispensable role on the ground. Amid ongoing tensions and regional instability, the Mission remains vital for monitoring the situation, preventing further escalation, and providing the necessary foundation for the political process. We welcome the continuation of a full one-year mandate, which ensures operational predictability and allows MINURSO to effectively carry out its duties, including unrestricted movement and safe resupply of its team sites.

Denmark reaffirms its steadfast support for the United Nations-led political process and for the Personal Envoy of the Secretary-General, Mr. Staffan de Mistura. We urge all parties—Morocco, the Frente POLISARIO, Algeria, and Mauritania—to re-engage in negotiations in good faith, without preconditions, and in a spirit of compromise to achieve a just, lasting, and mutually acceptable political solution in accordance with relevant Security Council resolutions.

In this context, Denmark considers the autonomy proposal presented by Morocco in 2007 to be a serious and credible contribution to the UN-led process and a realistic basis for negotiations between the parties. At the same time, we wish to make clear that Denmark’s vote in favour of today’s resolution does not constitute recognition of Moroccan sovereignty over Western Sahara. We maintain that a definitive and lasting settlement must be agreed upon by the parties and provide for the self-determination of the people of Western Sahara, consistent with the principles and purposes of the Charter of the United Nations.

Finally, Denmark reiterates the crucial importance of full respect for international law, including international human rights law and international humanitarian law. We welcome the resolution’s call for enhanced cooperation with the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights, including through facilitating visits to the region, and we express our continued concern for the humanitarian situation of the Sahrawi refugees in Tindouf, calling for sustained international support.

Thank you.
after.France:
Mr. President,

France welcomes the adoption of the resolution renewing the mandate of MINURSO for an additional twelve months. We thank the United States, as penholder, for its efforts to conduct constructive consultations and achieve a text that reflects the necessary political momentum.

By adopting this resolution, the Security Council has once again reaffirmed its commitment to stability in the region and to a realistic, viable, and lasting political solution. We reiterate our full support for the Personal Envoy of the Secretary-General, Mr. Staffan de Mistura, whose tireless efforts are essential to revitalizing the political process. We urge all parties—Morocco, the Frente POLISARIO, Algeria, and Mauritania—to commit to the negotiations convened under his auspices, in good faith, without preconditions, and building upon the achievements of recent discussions.

MINURSO plays an indispensable role in maintaining peace and stability on the ground. We recall the necessity of ensuring full and unhindered freedom of movement for the Mission and guaranteeing the regular resupply of its team sites. France also reiterates its call for a complete cessation of hostilities and full respect for the ceasefire, as any breach jeopardizes the prospects for a political settlement and puts civilian populations at risk.

France’s position on Western Sahara is clear, constant, and well known: the present and future of Western Sahara lie within the framework of Moroccan sovereignty. The Autonomy Plan presented by Morocco in 2007 constitutes the only serious, credible, and realistic basis for achieving a just, lasting, and mutually acceptable negotiated political solution, in accordance with the resolutions of this Council. There is today a growing and decisive international momentum in favor of this approach, and France remains fully engaged alongside its partners to help bring this long-standing dispute to an end.

Finally, we express our continued concern over the humanitarian situation in the Tindouf refugee camps, and we reiterate the importance of mobilizing adequate humanitarian assistance while repeating the Council's call for the registration of refugees.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.Greece:
Thank you, Mr. President.

Greece voted in favour of the resolution just adopted, which extends the mandate of MINURSO for an additional year, until 31 October 2027. We thank the United States, as the penholder, for its dedicated efforts and leadership in steering the negotiations on this text.

after.Liberia:

after.Pakistan:
Mr. President,

Pakistan abstained in the voting on the resolution just adopted. 

Our vote reflects Pakistan’s principled and consistent position on the question of Western Sahara, which has guided our approach across decades of Security Council deliberations. Pakistan attaches immense importance to an early, peaceful, and durable settlement of this dispute, which involves countries and peoples with whom we share deep, historic, and fraternal ties.

Pakistan has consistently advocated for a just, lasting, and mutually acceptable political solution, reached through negotiations without preconditions, that provides for the realization of the right to self-determination of the people of Western Sahara, in conformity with the principles and purposes of the Charter of the United Nations and relevant Security Council resolutions. 

For Pakistan, the cardinal principle of self-determination, enshrined in the UN Charter and grounded in international law, is sacrosanct. It cannot be compromised, diluted, or pre-judged. While we acknowledge the dedicated efforts of the penholder, the United States, to inject momentum into the political process, the text adopted today continues to tilt the balance and does not adequately reflect the established parameters set by previous Council resolutions, nor does it fully encompass the positions of all parties concerned. A durable solution cannot be imposed; it can only be achieved through genuine compromise and mutual agreement between the parties.

At the same time, Pakistan reaffirms its full support for the United Nations Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara (MINURSO), whose presence remains vital for preserving stability on the ground and creating an environment conducive to political dialogue. We also reiterate our support for the Personal Envoy of the Secretary-General, Mr. Staffan de Mistura, and urge all parties to engage constructively and in good faith with his facilitation efforts to achieve a peaceful and just resolution.

I thank you.
after.Panama:

after.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,

The Russian Federation abstained in the voting on the draft resolution prepared by the United States extending the mandate of the United Nations Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara (MINURSO).

Our position on the Western Sahara settlement is well known, principled, and consistent. Russia has consistently advocated for a balanced, objective, and impartial approach to this long-standing issue. We remain convinced that a just, lasting, and mutually acceptable political solution can only be achieved on the basis of relevant Security Council resolutions, within the framework of principles and purposes of the Charter of the United Nations, and through direct negotiations between Morocco and the Frente POLISARIO, with the support of the international community. Such a solution must provide for the self-determination of the people of Western Sahara.

Unfortunately, the resolution just adopted cannot be considered balanced. Once again, the informal penholder of the dossier has chosen to use Council resolutions to promote its own national foreign policy preferences, rather than working to build a genuine consensus among Council members. Pre-determining the final outcome of the negotiation process by attempting to impose a single template or prioritizing one proposal over others undermines the role of the Security Council as an honest broker and does not facilitate the resumption of constructive direct talks. 

We note with regret that the established working methods of the Council continue to be eroded. Substantive proposals aimed at restoring balance and reaffirming the internationally recognized parameters of the settlement were once again sidelined. 

At the same time, our abstention confirms Russia’s continued support for the United Nations Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara, which plays a key stabilizing role on the ground, as well as our support for the efforts of the Personal Envoy of the Secretary-General, Mr. Staffan de Mistura. We call on all parties to exercise restraint, adhere strictly to the ceasefire, and engage in good-faith dialogue without preconditions to achieve a sustainable and just peace in the region.

Thank you.
after.Somalia:

after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
